key_insight: Low hydrogen partial pressure during reactive sputtering is the main process knob for making YHO thin films that stay more transparent, more photochromic, and bleach faster after illumination.
engineering_relevance: For AI solar cell and smart-window coatings, tuning the H2/Ar ratio offers a practical way to optimize optical performance and recovery speed during scalable thin-film deposition.
method: Reactive magnetron sputtering of yttrium hydride films over a wide H2/Ar flow ratio range
Post-oxidation in air to form oxygen-containing YHO films
In situ plasma optical emission spectroscopy plus XRD, transmittance, photochromic testing, and XPS characterization
evidence_signal: As H2/Ar increased from 0.08 to 0.60, photochromic contrast dropped from 14% to 7%, transmittance fell from about 85% to 70%, and bleaching time constants were fastest for films made at H2/Ar < 0.25.
watch_item: The reported trend is process- and thickness-dependent, so translation to other sputtering systems or thicker films may require re-optimization of hydrogen partial pressure and oxidation conditions.
paper_title: Hydrogen partial pressure as a key parameter in the reactive sputtering of photochromic YHO thin films
